# The mountain, the journey to confidence, and thirty hours

*A-159 · proposal for taste-check, 2026-08-18. Nothing applied — no live file touched.*

---

## (a) The journey metaphor: **FOUND**, not invented

You were right that we have got it. It is already in the app in three places, and it is already a mountain.

**1. The player's own backdrop is a mountain.** `LearningPlayer.vue` renders a `.mountain-silhouette` behind every session — a sumi-e ink landscape, layered ridgelines dissolving into cloud, a torii gate, a pagoda, old pines, three birds. It is drawn at `--mountain-opacity: 0.18`, a token that exists in `design-tokens.css` for exactly this. So the mountain is *literally* the backdrop of the app already, and has been for a while.

**2. `PlanPanel.vue` already says the sentence.** On the Me screen, under "How you want to do it":

> "Thirty hours is the stretch that matters. **How you climb it is completely up to you — same mountain, different routes up.**"

Its code comment says the same thing: *"Every route adds up to the same thirty hours. Same mountain, different paths."* The five cadence choices are literally called **routes**. The progress bar underneath is a CSS class called `.trail`, and it only ever draws ground covered — never the remainder.

**3. The explainer prose reaches for the same imagery.** In `learnerExplainers.ts`: five-minutes-a-day is *"the hardest road of the lot"*; the pause is *"laying down the path that makes it come next time"*.

**What does NOT exist:** any *drawn* journey. The mountain is decorative wallpaper behind the player, and the climb is a flat 4px bar on the Me screen. The metaphor is written but never pictured, and Fast/Easy has never been connected to it at all. That gap is the whole of what this proposal fills.

*(Checked and ruled out: the belt progression is a martial-arts ladder, not a journey; the constellation view is a network, not a path; `useLearnerJourney.ts` is an old stats RPC carrying evolution scores and points — dead against the founder ruling and not learner-facing; schools' `JourneyBar.vue` is a teacher-facing progress bar labelled "Course Journey".)*

## (b) The treatment

![The climb — phone mockup at 390px](data:image/png;base64,)

*Mockup, real Mist tokens, 390px phone width. Source: `docs/a159-mountain-mockup/mountain.html`.*

Three things, one idea:

**The climb gets drawn.** The flat `.trail` bar becomes the ridgeline the player already carries, with the path inked onto it. Ground covered is drawn in the one belt colour; ground ahead is a faint dotted line. Nothing counts down and no percentage is spoken — same discipline as the bar it replaces.

**Thirty hours is the scale of the climb, not a headline.** It appears once, 9.5px, grey, next to the far mark on the ridge: *thirty hours*. It is where the path is going, the way a summit name sits on a map. The founder ruling holds — it stays quiet and inside the methodology.

**Fast and Easy become the pace you walk it, not a second route.** This is the one place I have deliberately bent your dictation, and it is the crux of the whole thing, so here is the reasoning in full.

### Why not "the fast way up" and "the easy way up"

Two separate problems, and they compound:

1. **"The easy way up a mountain" means the soft option in English.** No amount of surrounding copy repairs that. Easy is not a lesser climb — it is *more* thinking time and *more* repetition, which is genuinely more work per phrase, not less. Naming it "the easy route up" tells the learner the opposite of the truth about it.
2. **"Route" is already taken, by you.** `PlanPanel` calls the cadence choices routes — an hour a day, a real burn, weekends only. If Fast/Easy also become routes up the same mountain, the learner has two different things called routes, on the same screen, meaning different things. The metaphor stops carrying anything.

Both dissolve if the mountain stays **the thirty hours**, the route stays **how you spread the climb**, and Fast/Easy become **how you walk** — your stride. Nobody hears a judgement in a walking pace: the person taking longer strides is not better at the mountain than the person taking more of them, and both are on exactly the same path covering exactly the same ground. It keeps your intent — same summit, two ways, neither the lesser — and dodges both traps.

**If you want the literal two-paths version anyway, say so and I will draw it** — two lines forking and rejoining at the summit. It is prettier and it is the thing you actually described. I think it costs you the non-judgemental reading, which is why I have not led with it.

## (c) Every word I would change, side by side

Only two edits. Both are additions; nothing existing is rewritten.

### 1. `learnerExplainers.ts` → HOW_THIS_WORKS_LEARNER → "The different ways to use it"

| | |
|---|---|
| **Now** | "Speaking is the main one, and it is what you get by default. Easy and Fast are the two paces, and you pick between them on the player screen before you start. Offline lives behind the sliders button at the bottom of the player, and Listening lives in Settings." |
| **Proposed** | *unchanged*, **plus a second paragraph:** "Easy and Fast are the same climb walked at two different paces. They cover the same ground and they arrive at the same place — Easy simply leaves you more room between the steps. Most people use both, depending on the day." |

The existing bullet — *"Fast is the standard pace. Easy gives you about double the thinking time and more repetition, for when you want longer to get the words out."* — stays **exactly as written**. It is doing the factual work; the new paragraph only does the framing.

### 2. `PlanPanel.vue` → one new line under the Fast/Easy pair

| | |
|---|---|
| **Now** | Fast/Easy is not on this screen at all. |
| **Proposed** | "Same path either way, and the same ground under you. Easy just leaves more room between the steps. Swap whenever the day changes." |

And the existing intro line — *"Thirty hours is the stretch that matters. How you climb it is completely up to you — same mountain, different routes up."* — **does not change**. It is the sentence the whole treatment is built to earn.

That is the lot. Three sentences of new prose in total.

---

## (d) Better × Simpler × Cheaper

**Better:** it pictures a metaphor the app already asserts in words, so the thirty hours becomes something the learner can see themselves partway along rather than a number they are told; **simpler:** it adds no new concept — the mountain, the routes, the trail and the thirty are all already here, and Fast/Easy stops being an orphan setting by joining them; **cheaper:** one inline SVG replacing a 4px div, three sentences of copy, no new data, no new request, no new surface to maintain.

---

## (e) Recommendation — answerable in one word

**My recommendation: YES, in the stride framing above.** The metaphor is already yours and already written; this only draws it, and it costs three sentences.

Pick one:

- **YES** — build it as shown: drawn climb on the Me screen, thirty hours as the far mark, Fast/Easy as the pace you walk it, three new sentences.
- **PATHS** — you want the literal two-forking-paths version despite the soft-option reading; I will draw that instead and you judge them side by side.
- **PICTURE** — draw the climb, but leave every word alone; no copy change at all.
- **NO** — leave it. The flat trail bar and the existing sentence are enough, and the drawing is decoration we would have to keep.

Also dropped: any climbing-progress percentage, remainder, or distance-to-summit readout — the ruling against countdowns and things that can be missed applies to a drawn path exactly as it does to a bar.*
